name: the state a surface is in before it is worked over again
function: It is a real object, made properly, and it is not the last thing that will happen to this surface. Everything on it will be gone over — buried, scraped back, contradicted — by the same person, later, and only some of it will still be visible when that has happened. It is looked at now, hard, by somebody deciding what to do to it next. It is not a sketch: a sketch is a proposal for another object, and this is the object, in an earlier state of itself.
consequences: It will be destroyed by its own maker and this is not a failure. Every mark is made in the knowledge that it is provisional, and a mark made to survive is a mark refusing the condition of the thing it is part of.

Some of it will show through and the maker does not get to choose which. What is under a later layer is not gone; it edits the thing above it, so decisions taken now go on acting after they stop being visible.

It is read as a set of options rather than as a resolution. The only viewer is looking for where to go next, so a passage that closes everything down is worth less here than one that is wrong in a way that suggests the next move.
There is no finish and no moment of completion. It stops when it is left, and being left is a state it may be in for an afternoon or for six years.
It has no audience and no occasion, so nothing in it can be doing the work of arrival. It does not have to survive being seen from anywhere, in any light, by anybody.

Its whole surface is available and none of it is protected. Anything can be gone over, including the best thing on it, and the best thing on it is the most likely to be defended past the point where defending it is honest.
It exists in one copy in one state, and that state is not recorded. Once it is worked over, the thing described here is unrecoverable, and nobody will ever be able to check what it looked like.
It is compared with nothing except what it becomes. There is no other object of its kind to be better or worse than, and the only judgement available is whether the next state needed this one.
doesNotDecide: Composition, palette, imagery, type, scale, how much of the surface is used, how far it is taken, what will be buried, and what any of it is about. None of that follows from it being an earlier state.
